newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani agency puts ICI's certificate on watch.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani agency puts ICI's certificate on watch.

text.p: Pakistan's Credit Rating Agency (PACRA) said on Tuesday it had put term finance certificates (TFCs) of ICI Pakistan Ltd 's PTA plant on "rating watch" after its acquisition by U.S.-based DuPont.
"Consequent upon the reported acquisition of ICI's PTA (pure terephthalic acid) plant by Dupont, PACRA has placed ICI's TFC's on rating watch," a PACRA statement said.
ICI Pakistan, a subsidiary of ICI Plc, said on Tuesday it intended to enter into a joint venture agreement with DuPont for the PTA plant being constructed in Karachi.
DuPont on Monday picked up a 50 percent stake in ICI Pakistan as part of a global deal to buy half of ICI Plc's bulk chemical business for $3 billion.
PACRA said it had rated the TFCs AA on its affiliation with and support from ICI Plc.

"The change in the ownership per se is not a matter of concern given the global standing and financial strength of the DuPont group as reflected in the international rating of Aa3 (assigned by Moody's)," it said.

"However, PACRA would like to examine full details of the terms of the proposed acquisition before assigning a new rating to the TFCs, the liability for which shall be assumed by the new entity," it added.
ICI Pakistan said the joint venture proposal would be considered for approval by the board of directors of ICI Pakistan at its meeting on August 12.

ICI Pakistan, listed on the Karachi Stock Exchange with a paid up capital of 7.871 billion rupees ($193.77 million), is currently owned 61 percent by ICI Plc. It manufactures polyester staple fibre, soda ash, paints, pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, explosives, some consumer items and other speciality chemicals.
ICI had planned to start commercial production at its $450 million PTA plant near Karachi's Port Qasim by November 1997.
The plant will manufacture 400,000 tonnes of PTA, a raw material used in making polyester staple fibre, to be sold in Pakistan and abroad.
